question: The Earth has been divided into many time zones. How many degrees does each time zone covers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15 degrees.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth completes one full rotation of 360° on its axis in 24 hours. (पृथ्वी की घूर्णन गति)

 

• To standardize time globally, the world is divided into 24 time zones, one for each hour of the day.

 

• Dividing 360° by 24 hours gives 360 ÷ 24 = 15° of longitude per time zone, meaning every 15° of longitude corresponds to a one-hour difference in local time.

 

• This is why time changes by roughly one hour for every 15° you travel east or west, and this system underlies the concept of Standard Time Zones used by countries worldwide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India follows a single time zone based on the 82.5° E longitude (passing near Mirzapur, UP), known as Indian Standard Time (IST), which is UTC +5:30.

 

• Countries with large east-west extent, like Russia and the USA, span multiple time zones (11 and several respectively).

 

NOTE

 

• 10 degrees (Option 1): Incorrect; this does not correspond to 360°/24 and has no standard basis in time-zone division.

 

• 20 degrees (Option 3): Incorrect; 20° per zone would only allow for 18 zones (360/20), not the standard 24.

 

• 24 degrees (Option 4): Incorrect; this confuses the number of time zones (24) with the degree width of each zone.

question: Pandit Ram Narayan is a Hindustani Classical musician who plays ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ram Narayan was a legendary Hindustani classical musician renowned as a Sarangi maestro. (सारंगी वादक)

 

• He is widely credited with elevating the sarangi from an accompanying instrument to a respected solo concert instrument in Indian classical music.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2005), India's second-highest civilian award, along with the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan earlier in his career, and received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

• The sarangi is a short-necked, bowed string instrument traditionally used to accompany vocal music, known for its ability to closely mimic the human voice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• His son, Pandit Bharat Bhushan Goswami, has also carried forward the sarangi tradition.

 

• Other noted sarangi players include Ustad Sultan Khan and Pandit Ram Narayan's contemporaries in the Hindustani classical tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Tabla (Option 2): A pair of hand drums; famous tabla players include Ustad Zakir Hussain and Pandit Kishan Maharaj, not Ram Narayan.

 

• Flute (Option 3): A wind instrument (bansuri); Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a celebrated flute (bansuri) player.

 

• Harmonium (Option 4): A keyboard reed instrument; it is not the instrument Ram Narayan was known for.

question: Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled 14 feet high statue of Lok Nayak Jayprakash Narayan in ______ in October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled a 14-feet high statue of Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) at his birthplace, Sitab Diara village, Saran district, Bihar, in October 2022. (लोकनायक जयप्रकाश नारायण)

 

• The unveiling took place on 11 October 2022, marking JP's 120th birth anniversary.

 

• Jayaprakash Narayan was a freedom fighter and socialist political leader, famously known for leading the Total Revolution (Sampoorna Kranti) movement against the Indira Gandhi government in the 1970s.

 

• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999 for his contributions to Indian democracy and social reform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• JP played a key role in the Quit India Movement (1942) and later founded the Sarvodaya movement inspired by Gandhian principles.

 

• Sitab Diara straddles the Bihar–Uttar Pradesh border along the Ganga and Ghaghara rivers, and is JP's ancestral village.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Not the location; the statue was unveiled in Bihar, JP's home state.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Not the location of the unveiling.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4): Not the location of the unveiling.

question: The first woman to win the Dronacharya Award was weightlifting coach ______ in 2000.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hansa Sharma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hansa Sharma, a weightlifting coach, became the first woman to receive the Dronacharya Award in the year 2000. (द्रोणाचार्य पुरस्कार)

 

• The Dronacharya Award is India's highest honour for sports coaches, instituted in 1985 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, named after Dronacharya, the guru of the Kauravas and Pandavas in the Mahabharata.

 

• It recognises coaches who have produced medal-winning performances at international competitions such as the Olympics, World Championships, and Asian Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first-ever Dronacharya Award recipients (1985) included coaches like Bhalachandra Bhagwat and O. M. Nambiar.

 

• Later prominent women Dronacharya awardees include Purnima Mahato (archery coach).

 

NOTE

 

• Renu Kohli (Option 2): Not the first woman to win the award; not associated with this particular distinction.

 

• Sunita Sharma (Option 3): A different individual; not the first woman Dronacharya awardee.

 

• Purnima Mahato (Option 4): A well-known archery coach and Dronacharya awardee (2001), but not the first woman recipient — that distinction belongs to Hansa Sharma in 2000.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct?
I. Death rate in India is 7.2 per 1000 in 2011.
II. Life expectancy at birth is 72.6 years in 2012.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I — India's death rate declined steadily from about 25 per 1000 population in 1951 to around 7.1–7.2 per 1000 in 2011, reflecting improvements in healthcare, sanitation, and nutrition. This statement is correct. (मृत्यु दर)

 

• Statement II — India's life expectancy at birth in 2012 was actually around 66–68 years, not 72.6 years as claimed. This statement is therefore incorrect.

 

• Since only the first statement holds true, the correct choice is "Only I".

 

• These indicators — birth rate, death rate, and life expectancy — are tracked by the Sample Registration System (SRS) of the Office of the Registrar General of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's life expectancy has continued to rise since 2012, crossing 69–70 years in later SRS reports (2015–19 period).

 

• The declining death rate and rising life expectancy together reflect India's ongoing demographic transition.

 

NOTE

 

• Both I and II (Option 1): Incorrect, because Statement II's figure (72.6 years) does not match the actual 2012 life expectancy data.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement I's death-rate figure is accurate for 2011.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement II is the false one, not Statement I.

question: When lead nitrate is heated, then which of the following gases is produced?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen dioxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When lead nitrate [Pb(NO₃)₂] is heated strongly, it undergoes thermal decomposition, producing lead oxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) gas, and oxygen (O₂) gas. (नाइट्रोजन डाइऑक्साइड)

 

• The balanced chemical equation is:

 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂↑ + O₂↑

 

• This reaction is a classic example of decomposition reaction and is notable for producing brown fumes of NO₂, along with a crackling sound — often demonstrated in chemistry labs.

 

• Lead oxide (PbO), a yellow solid, remains behind as the residue after heating.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Most nitrates of heavy metals (like lead, copper, zinc) decompose on heating to give the metal oxide, NO₂, and O₂, unlike alkali metal nitrates, which usually decompose to give the nitrite and O₂.

 

• This lead nitrate decomposition reaction is sometimes called the "Nitrogen Dioxide/Lead monoxide fumes" reaction, popularly demonstrated as a small explosive crackling reaction in a test tube.

 

NOTE

 

• Lead oxide (Option 2): This is the solid residue left behind after heating, not the gas produced.

 

• Nitrogen oxide (Option 3): Not the gas produced in this specific reaction; the gas evolved is nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), not nitrogen monoxide (NO).

 

• Lead dioxide (Option 4): Not a product of this reaction; the solid residue formed is lead monoxide (PbO), not lead dioxide (PbO₂).

question: What are hardware devices that retrieves data from a computer system and further translates the received data into a form understandable to humans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Output Devices.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Output devices are hardware components that retrieve/receive data (results) from a computer system and convert them into a human-understandable form, such as text, images, sound, or printed material. (आउटपुट डिवाइस)

 

• Common examples of output devices include monitors, printers, speakers, plotters, and projectors.

 

• They form the final stage of the Input–Process–Output (IPO) cycle of computing, presenting the processed results back to the user.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some devices, like touchscreens and modems, act as both input and output devices (I/O devices).

 

• The processed "output" can be in various forms — soft copy (displayed on screen) or hard copy (printed on paper).

 

NOTE

 

• Storage Devices (Option 1): These are used to store data permanently or temporarily (e.g., hard disk, pen drive), not to translate data for humans.

 

• Processor (Option 2): The CPU processes and executes instructions/data; it does not present data in human-understandable form directly.

 

• Input Devices (Option 3): These are used to feed data/instructions into the computer (e.g., keyboard, mouse), the opposite function of an output device.

question: In which year was Battle of Peshawar fought between Raja Jayapal and Mahmud Ghazni?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1001.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Peshawar was fought in 1001 CE between Raja Jayapala, the Hindu Shahi ruler, and Mahmud of Ghazni. (महमूद गजनवी बनाम राजा जयपाल)

 

• This was Mahmud of Ghazni's first major invasion of the Indian subcontinent and marked the beginning of a long series of raids into northern India.

 

• Jayapala was defeated in this battle and was captured, but later released; humiliated by the defeat, he abdicated in favour of his son Anandapala and later took his own life.

 

• The Hindu Shahi kingdom, centred around Peshawar and the Kabul valley, was the principal frontier power resisting the early Ghaznavid invasions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahmud of Ghazni went on to lead a total of 17 invasions into India between 1000 and 1027 CE, the most infamous being the raid on the Somnath Temple in 1025.

 

• Jayapala's son Anandapala continued resistance against the Ghaznavids, notably at the Battle of Chach (Waihind) in 1008–09.

 

NOTE

 

• 1112 (Option 1): Not the correct year; no major Jayapala–Mahmud Ghazni battle is dated to this year.

 

• 1305 (Option 2): This is much later, during the Delhi Sultanate period, unrelated to Mahmud Ghazni's invasions.

 

• 1258 (Option 4): This year is associated with the fall of Baghdad to the Mongols, not this battle.

question: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Act made the Right to education a Fundamental Right under article 21 A of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A into the Indian Constitution, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years. (शिक्षा का अधिकार)

 

• It states: "The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine."

 

• This amendment also added a corresponding Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k), requiring parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children.

 

• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 was subsequently enacted to give practical effect to Article 21A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Before the 86th Amendment, the Right to Education existed only as a Directive Principle of State Policy under Article 45.

 

• After the amendment, Article 45 was revised to focus on early childhood care and education for children below 6 years.

 

NOTE

 

• 89th Amendment Act, 2003 (Option 1): This amendment provided for the bifurcation of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into two separate commissions.

 

• 19th Amendment Act, 1966 (Option 2): This amendment dealt with the abolition of the Election Tribunals and transferred election petition matters to High Courts.

 

• 91st Amendment Act, 2003 (Option 4): This amendment limited the size of the Council of Ministers and addressed anti-defection provisions.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to make the contents of a cell italic in MS-Excel 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS-Excel, the shortcut Ctrl + 3 is used to apply or remove italic formatting to the contents of a selected cell. (इटैलिक फॉर्मेटिंग)

 

• Excel also supports the more widely known Ctrl + I shortcut for the same italic-toggle function; Ctrl+3 is an alternate numeric formatting shortcut.

 

• Excel's related numeric-key formatting shortcuts include: Ctrl+1 (Format Cells dialog), Ctrl+2 (Bold), Ctrl+3 (Italic), Ctrl+4 (Underline), and Ctrl+5 (Strikethrough).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• These numeric-key shortcuts (Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+5) work consistently across most versions of Excel, including Excel 365.

 

• Similar text-formatting shortcuts (Ctrl+B for bold, Ctrl+U for underline) are also standard across Microsoft Office applications.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + 4 (Option 1): This applies/removes underline formatting, not italic.

 

• Ctrl + 6 (Option 3): This is used to toggle the display of objects (like images/charts) on the worksheet, not for italics.

 

• Ctrl + 2 (Option 4): This applies/removes bold formatting, not italic.

question: Which country will host the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is France.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• France hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games in its capital city, Paris. (2024 ग्रीष्मकालीन ओलंपिक)

 

• This marked the third time Paris hosted the Summer Olympics, following 1900 and 1924 — making Paris only the second city (after London) to host the Games three times.

 

• The 2024 Games featured a unique opening ceremony held along the Seine River, rather than in a traditional stadium, and also saw the debut of breaking (breakdance) as an Olympic sport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2028 Summer Olympics are scheduled to be held in Los Angeles, USA, and the 2032 Games in Brisbane, Australia.

 

• India's contingent at Paris 2024 won a total of 6 medals (1 silver, 5 bronze).

 

NOTE

 

• Germany (Option 1): Not the host; Germany last hosted the Summer Olympics in Munich in 1972.

 

• Switzerland (Option 3): Not an Olympic host in this cycle; Switzerland has never hosted a Summer Olympics.

 

• England (Option 4): Not the host in 2024; London (England) last hosted the Summer Olympics in 2012.

question: Which of the following sports was NOT played at Tokyo Olympics 2020 held in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mallakhamba.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mallakhamba is a traditional Indian sport involving gymnastic and yogic postures performed on a vertical wooden pole, cane, or rope, and it has never been part of the Olympic Games programme. (मल्लखंब — पारंपरिक भारतीय खेल)

 

• The Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic) featured 33 sports, including Table Tennis, Volleyball, and Fencing, all of which are long-standing Olympic disciplines.

 

• Tokyo 2020 also introduced new sports to the Olympic programme such as Skateboarding, Surfing, Sport Climbing, and Karate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• There have been ongoing efforts and demands in India to get Mallakhamba recognised internationally and eventually included in future Olympic Games.

 

• Tokyo 2020 was the first Olympics to be postponed (rather than cancelled) in modern Olympic history.

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 2): Contested at Tokyo 2020; India's table tennis paddlers, including veteran Achanta Sharath Kamal, competed there.

 

• Volleyball (Option 3): A standard Olympic sport contested at Tokyo 2020, including both indoor and beach volleyball formats.

 

• Fencing (Option 4): A core Olympic sport contested at Tokyo 2020; India's Bhavani Devi became the first Indian fencer to qualify for the Olympics that year.

question: Who of the following person wrote a book named Kitab-ul-Hind?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Al-Biruni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kitab-ul-Hind (also known as Tahqiq-i-Hind) was written by Al-Biruni, an 11th-century Persian polymath who accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India. (अल-बिरूनी की कृति)

 

• The book is a detailed and relatively objective account of Indian society, religion, philosophy, science, astronomy, and customs of that period, based on Al-Biruni's own observations and study of Sanskrit texts.

 

• Al-Biruni is considered one of the earliest scholars to study Indian civilization systematically and is often regarded as a pioneer of comparative religious and cultural studies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Al-Biruni was also a noted mathematician, astronomer, and geographer, and made significant contributions to understanding the shape and dimensions of the Earth.

 

• He learned Sanskrit and studied works such as the Bhagavad Gita and texts on Indian astronomy to compile his account.

 

NOTE

 

• Antara Ibn Shaddad (Option 1): A pre-Islamic Arab poet and warrior, famous for his poetry (Mu'allaqat), not associated with Kitab-ul-Hind.

 

• Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (Option 2): Another pre-Islamic Arab poet, one of the authors of the Mu'allaqat, unrelated to this work.

 

• Imru' al-Qais (Option 3): A celebrated pre-Islamic Arabian poet, considered a founder of Arabic poetry, but not the author of Kitab-ul-Hind.

question: What is the official language of Bhutan, a neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dzongkha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dzongkha is the official national language of Bhutan. (भूटान की राष्ट्रभाषा)

 

• It is a Sino-Tibetan language, closely related to Tibetan, and is written using the Tibetan script.

 

• Bhutan is a landlocked country in the eastern Himalayas, bordered by India to the south, east, and west, and China (Tibet) to the north.

 

• Its capital is Thimphu, and its official currency is the Ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian Rupee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhutan is known for measuring development through Gross National Happiness (GNH) instead of relying solely on GDP.

 

• Bhutan became a parliamentary democracy in 2008 under King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck.

 

NOTE

 

• Kyat (Option 1): This is the currency of Myanmar, not a language.

 

• Yuan (Option 2): This is the currency of China (Renminbi), not a language.

 

• Ngultrum (Option 3): This is the currency of Bhutan, not its language.

question: The monetary policy instrument called ‘bank rate’ is aligned to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marginal standing facility rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bank Rate, the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends long-term funds to commercial banks without any collateral, is aligned to (kept equal to) the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate. (बैंक दर)

 

• This alignment was introduced by the RBI in May 2011, as part of reforms to make the interest-rate framework more consistent and transparent.

 

• Both the Bank Rate and the MSF rate move in tandem with the repo rate; whenever the repo rate changes, the MSF rate (and consequently the Bank Rate) is adjusted accordingly, typically kept 25 basis points above the repo rate.

 

• The Bank Rate is also used as a penal rate under Sections 24 and 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, for banks that fail to maintain the required Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) or Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The MSF was introduced by the RBI in 2011 to allow banks to borrow overnight funds against their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) securities, in emergency situations, at a rate higher than the repo rate.

 

• The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) comprises the repo and reverse repo rates, distinct instruments used for short-term liquidity management.

 

NOTE

 

• Cash Reserve ratio (Option 1): The percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be kept with the RBI in cash form; it is a separate monetary policy tool, not linked to the Bank Rate.

 

• Liquidity adjustment facility (Option 2): This mechanism (comprising repo/reverse repo) is used for day-to-day liquidity management, distinct from the Bank Rate-MSF linkage.

 

• Discount rate (Option 3): This term is generally used interchangeably with "Bank Rate" in some contexts internationally, but as an option distinct from Bank Rate here, it is not the correct match — the Bank Rate is specifically pegged to the MSF rate in India's current framework.

question:
The simultaneous shifts of both the demand curve and the supply curve can happen in which of the following ways?
I. Supply curve shifts leftward and demand curve shifts rightward.
II. Both supply and demand curves shift leftwards.
III. Supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward.
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II and III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The demand curve shifts due to changes in non-price determinants of demand (income, tastes, prices of related goods, etc.), while the supply curve shifts due to changes in non-price determinants of supply (input costs, technology, number of sellers, etc.). (माँग वक्र एवं पूर्ति वक्र में परिवर्तन)

 

• Since these two sets of determinants are independent of each other, both curves can shift simultaneously in any direction relative to one another — in the same direction or in opposite directions.

 

• Statement I (supply shifts left, demand shifts right), Statement II (both shift left), and Statement III (supply shifts right, demand shifts left) are all theoretically valid and possible combinations of simultaneous shifts.

 

• Each combination leads to different, sometimes ambiguous, effects on equilibrium price and quantity, which is a key concept studied in the theory of simultaneous shifts in demand and supply.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• When both curves shift in the same direction, the effect on equilibrium quantity is predictable, but the effect on price is ambiguous (depends on the relative magnitude of shifts).

 

• When both curves shift in opposite directions, the effect on equilibrium price is predictable, but the effect on quantity is ambiguous.

 

NOTE

 

• II and III (Option 2): Incomplete; this excludes Statement I, which is also a valid possible combination of simultaneous shifts.

 

• I and II (Option 3): Incomplete; this excludes Statement III, which is also a valid possible combination.

 

• Only I (Option 4): Incomplete; this considers only one of the three valid combinations, ignoring that II and III are equally possible.

question: Which state hosted the 36th National Games in the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gujarat hosted the 36th National Games of India in September–October 2022. (36वें राष्ट्रीय खेल)

 

• These were the first National Games held after an eight-year gap (the previous edition, the 35th National Games, was held in Kerala in 2015) and the first ever to be hosted by Gujarat.

 

• The Games were held across multiple cities in Gujarat, including Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, and Rajkot, and featured a record number of participating athletes and sporting disciplines.

 

• Services Sports Control Board topped the medal tally, with Maharashtra finishing among the top-performing states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Games are organised by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and serve as a major multi-sport event within the country, similar in structure to the Olympic Games.

 

• The mascot for the 36th National Games was "Savaj", a stylised Asiatic lion, reflecting Gujarat's Gir forest heritage.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 1): Was set to host the 37th National Games (later postponed/rescheduled), not the 36th edition.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Did not host the 36th National Games, though it fielded a strong contingent.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Was not the host state for the 36th National Games.

question: Which amendment in the Indian constitution is related to extension of jurisdiction of High Courts to Union territories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7th Amendment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 is related to the extension of jurisdiction of High Courts to Union Territories, through the insertion/amendment of Article 230. (7वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम)

 

• This amendment was enacted primarily to give effect to the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission, restructuring Indian states along linguistic lines.

 

• Along with reorganizing states, it empowered Parliament to extend or restrict the jurisdiction of a High Court to any Union Territory, and to establish common High Courts for two or more states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 7th Amendment also introduced the classification of states into Part A, B, C, and D, subsequently replaced with a simpler classification of States and Union Territories.

 

• It also inserted Article 258A, permitting Union Territories to work with the Union executive in certain matters.

 

NOTE

 

• 9th Amendment (Option 1): Relates to the transfer of certain territories to Pakistan as part of the border settlement following the Indo-Pak agreement (Berubari Union case-related adjustments).

 

• 13th Amendment (Option 3): Created the state of Nagaland, granting it special status under Article 371A.

 

• 1st Amendment (Option 4): Added the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution and imposed reasonable restrictions on the freedom of speech and expression under Article 19.

question: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance of ____________ in southern India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form that originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu, in southern India. (तमिलनाडु का शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• It is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, historically performed by temple dancers (Devadasis), and rooted in the Natya Shastra by sage Bharata Muni.

 

• The dance form is characterized by fixed upper torso, bent legs (Aramandi posture), intricate footwork, and expressive hand gestures (mudras) and facial expressions (abhinaya).

 

• Renowned exponents of Bharatanatyam include Rukmini Devi Arundale, who revived and popularized the form in the 20th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's eight recognised classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• Bharatanatyam performances are traditionally accompanied by Carnatic music.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Home to classical dance forms Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, not Bharatanatyam.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for Yakshagana, a traditional dance-drama, not Bharatanatyam.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Home to the classical dance form Kuchipudi, not Bharatanatyam.

question: In which month, Hiroshima Day is observed across the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is August.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hiroshima Day is observed every year on 6th August, marking the anniversary of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, Japan, by the United States in 1945, during World War II. (हिरोशिमा दिवस)

 

• It is commemorated globally as a day to remember the devastating human cost of nuclear warfare and to promote peace and nuclear disarmament.

 

• The bombing of Hiroshima was followed three days later, on 9th August 1945, by the atomic bombing of Nagasaki, commemorated as Nagasaki Day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Both bombings led to Japan's surrender on 15 August 1945, effectively ending World War II.

 

• The Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, preserved as a symbol of peace.

 

NOTE

 

• July (Option 2): Incorrect; Hiroshima Day is not observed in July.

 

• January (Option 3): Incorrect; not associated with the Hiroshima bombing anniversary.

 

• October (Option 4): Incorrect; not the month of the Hiroshima bombing.

question: ISRO successfully launched the communication satellite GSAT-24 from _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kourou in French Guiana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ISRO's GSAT-24 communication satellite was successfully launched on 23 June 2022 aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou, French Guiana. (कोउरू, फ्रेंच गुयाना)

 

• GSAT-24 is a 24-Ku band transponder communication satellite, built entirely for Tata Play (formerly Tata Sky) through NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), the commercial arm of ISRO, marking the first satellite built on a "demand-driven" basis for a customer.

 

• The launch was carried out by Arianespace, a French launch service provider, as ISRO's heavier communication satellites are often launched from Kourou due to the Ariane rocket's higher payload capacity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Guiana Space Centre is strategically located near the equator, which provides an efficiency advantage for launching geostationary satellites.

 

• ISRO's own heavy-lift launch vehicle, the GSLV Mk III (LVM3), has since been used for some heavier satellite payloads previously dependent on foreign launches.

 

NOTE

 

• Berlin in Germany (Option 2): Not a spaceport; Germany does not host orbital satellite launch facilities.

 

• Moscow in Russia (Option 3): Not the launch site; Russian launches typically occur from Baikonur or Vostochny Cosmodromes, not Moscow.

 

• Chicago in US (Option 4): Not a launch site; US satellite launches typically occur from Cape Canaveral or Vandenberg, not Chicago.

question: Dhupgarh peak is the highest point of which of the following States of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhupgarh is the highest peak of Madhya Pradesh, with an elevation of about 1,352 metres (4,429 feet). (धूपगढ़ चोटी)

 

• It is located in the Satpura Range, near the hill station of Pachmarhi, within the Satpura National Park, in the Hoshangabad (Narmadapuram) district of Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Dhupgarh is popular for sunrise and sunset viewpoints and is a notable trekking destination in central India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pachmarhi, often called the "Satpura ki Rani" (Queen of Satpura), is the only hill station in Madhya Pradesh.

 

• The highest peak of the neighbouring state Chhattisgarh is Gaurshankar (Gaur Lata), and Jharkhand's highest peak is Parasnath Hill.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Its highest peak is Parasnath Hill, not Dhupgarh.

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 2): Its highest peak is Gaurshankar (Gaur Lata), not Dhupgarh.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Its highest point is near the Himalayan foothill region (around Uttarkashi border areas prior to Uttarakhand's formation); Dhupgarh is not associated with UP.

question: ______ percent can be taken as the average value for the amount of organic matter that is present at each step of food chain and reaches the next level of consumers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On average, only about 10 percent of the organic matter (energy) present at one trophic level of a food chain is transferred to and available for the next level of consumers; the rest is lost as heat, used in respiration, or remains undigested. (दस प्रतिशत नियम)

 

• This principle is known as the "Ten Percent Law", first proposed by ecologist Raymond Lindeman in 1942.

 

• This progressive loss of energy at each trophic level explains why food chains are typically limited to only 4–5 trophic levels, and why the biomass/energy pyramid is generally upright, narrowing towards the top.

 

• For example, if producers (plants) have 1000 units of energy, only about 100 units reach primary consumers (herbivores), and only about 10 units reach secondary consumers (carnivores).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This law underlies why top carnivores (like tigers) are relatively few in number compared to primary producers in an ecosystem.

 

• The 10% law is a foundational concept in the study of ecological pyramids — of numbers, biomass, and energy.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 (Option 1): Not the standard value used for energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels.

 

• 20 (Option 3): Not the standard textbook figure; overstates the typical transfer efficiency.

 

• 2 (Option 4): Too low; understates the typical average energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels.

question: “SOVA Virus” which is recently seen in the news is a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is malware.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "SOVA Virus" refers to SOVA, a sophisticated Android banking trojan (malware) that gained attention in 2022 for targeting banking and financial apps to steal user credentials and financial data. (साइबर मालवेयर)

 

• SOVA disguises itself as legitimate apps (such as Chrome, Amazon, or antivirus apps) to trick users into installing it, after which it can log keystrokes, steal cookies, intercept OTPs, and even perform ransomware-style file encryption in later versions.

 

• India's CERT-In (Cyber Swachhta Kendra) issued advisories warning users, particularly of banking apps, about the SOVA malware threat.

 

• SOVA is unrelated to biological viruses; it is purely a piece of malicious software (malware).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• SOVA is part of a broader wave of Android banking trojans, alongside malware families like FluBot, Cerberus, and TeaBot, that emerged around the same period.

 

• Users are typically advised to download apps only from official app stores (like Google Play) to reduce the risk of such malware infections.

 

NOTE

 

• Variant of monkey virus (Option 1): Incorrect; SOVA is not related to Monkeypox or any biological virus.

 

• Variant of covid-19 (Option 2): Incorrect; SOVA has no connection to COVID-19 or any coronavirus variant.

 

• Virus found in cattle (Option 3): Incorrect; SOVA is not a biological/veterinary virus.

question:
Which of the following is correct regarding the respiration?
I. Regular traditional breathing exercise (pranayama) can increase the capacity of lungs to take in more air.
II. During inhalation, ribs move up and outwards and diaphragm moves down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Pranayama, a traditional breathing exercise practiced in yoga, involves controlled, deep breathing techniques that increase lung capacity over time by strengthening the respiratory muscles and improving oxygen exchange efficiency. (प्राणायाम)

 

• Statement II is also correct: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and moves downward, while the rib cage (ribs) moves upward and outward due to contraction of the external intercostal muscles — together, these movements increase the volume of the thoracic cavity, causing air to be drawn into the lungs.

 

• During exhalation, the reverse occurs — the diaphragm relaxes and moves up (becoming dome-shaped again), and the ribs move down and inward, decreasing thoracic volume and pushing air out.

 

• Since both statements accurately describe respiratory physiology, the correct answer is "Both I and II".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The diaphragm is the primary muscle of respiration, a dome-shaped sheet of muscle separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities.

 

• Regular pranayama practices, such as *Anulom Vilom* and *Kapalbhati*, are widely promoted for improving respiratory health and lung function.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete; Statement II is also physiologically correct, not just Statement I.

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete; Statement I is also correct, as pranayama does improve lung capacity.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect; both statements accurately describe recognized respiratory facts.
